subject: English
passage: Marine biologist Dr. Erin Montague was studying coral formations in the Caribbean Sea. While diving there, Montague observed numerous circular scars on the ocean floor. Montague believed the scars could have been created by ancient feeding behaviors of large marine animals that lived in the area centuries ago. Some of the more recent scars were found directly overlapping the older scars. This led Montague to think that the same feeding grounds had been used continuously for many generations.
prompt: According to the text, why does Montague think that the same feeding grounds had been used continuously for many generations?

choices.A: She observed numerous circular scars on the ocean floor.
choices.B: She discovered the scars in the Caribbean Sea.
choices.C: Some of the newer scars were found directly overlapping the older scars.
choices.D: Some of the scars were circular and others were oval-shaped.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because the text explicitly states that the overlapping pattern of newer scars on top of older scars was what led Montague to think the feeding grounds had been used continuously for many generations.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. While the text states that Montague observed numerous scars, this observation led her to believe the scars were from ancient feeding behaviors but did not specifically indicate continuous use over generations. Rather, it was the overlapping pattern that led to her conclusion about duration.
